<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #61189. `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` label each option by position. A choice named `C, A, D, B` is shown as `A: C`, `B: A` and so on, so a model that answers "B" picks the option named `A`. A score named `"1".."5"` is shown as `0: 1` to `4: 5`, so a model that answers with the level's own digit reads one level high.

This PR takes the labels from the option names when the names are labels already: distinct capital letters for a choice, single digits for a score. The rule lives in `QuestionType.labels()`, so every read strategy uses it. `/v1/decisions` gets the choice rule through `make_read_question()`. The example DiffusionGemma gateway gets a copy of the same rule.

Liquid d1 keeps the score format its checkpoint was trained on: the legend `0 1`, `1 2`, ... and the digits `0` to `n-1` as readout tokens. On d1-3B that format reads `"1".."5"` at -0.10 levels (34/40 exact), and own-digit labels read it at -0.40 (23/40).

## Claims

- A choice whose options are distinct single capital letters keeps those letters as labels, on `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions`. Other choices keep `A` to `Z` by position.
- A score whose levels are all single ASCII digits (`"1".."5"`, `"0".."4"`) keeps those digits as labels, and the prompt shows each level as its digit alone.
- Every other score scale (`"1 star"`, `"1".."10"`, `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent`, words) keeps main's labels and a byte-identical prompt.
- Liquid d1 keeps the checkpoint's positional score digits. Its choice codes already used single-letter option names.
- The answer shape does not change: `score`, `legend` and `probabilities` stay 0-indexed by position.

## Validation

Tests:

- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/ tests/entrypoints/openai/decisions/ -k "not e2e"` (CPU): 109 passed.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_structured_decisions_e2e.py tests/entrypoints/openai/decisions/test_decisions_e2e.py` (GPU, Qwen3-0.6B): 16 passed. The `C, A, D, B` quiz case fails on main (`{'key': 'A'} != {'key': 'B'}`).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, the pre-commit pin) pass on the changed files.

Accuracy through vLLM serving, main against this PR:

- Letter choices sent out of order, where the state names the right letter (24 cases): Qwen3-4B goes from 1/24 to 24/24 on `/v1/systemone` and on `/v1/decisions`. DiffusionGemma goes from 17-18/24 to 24/24 built in, and from 15-17/24 to 24/24 through the gateway.
- `"1".."5"` on Qwen3-4B goes from +0.42 to -0.22 levels (21/40 to 26/40 exact). On DiffusionGemma it goes from 34/40 to 37/40 exact.
- `"0".."4"` incident severity on the gateway goes from 7/10 to 9/10 exact.
- The other scales read the same on both builds, within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Accuracy measurements</summary>

Each cell is the mean signed error in levels, then exact matches. Positive means the read was too high. The rows of `"1".."10"` are rescaled to 0..4 before scoring.

The data set has 40 product reviews (8 per level, 1 to 5 stars), 10 incident tickets (2 per severity, 0 to 4), and 24 letter-key cases. A key case is a state such as `Quiz key: the correct answer is B.` and a choice with options `C, A, D, B` (or `D, C, B, A`, or `B, C, D, A`) and no descriptions. The in-order control (`A, B, C, D`) scored 8/8 on every build.

Every row was run twice. The two Qwen3-4B and d1 runs agree within 0.01 levels and one exact match. The gateway runs used noise seeds 42 and 7. Where the runs differ, both values are shown.

| path · model | scale | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | words | +0.09 (34/40) | +0.09 (34/40) |
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | `"1".."5"` | +0.42 (21/40) | -0.22 (26/40) |
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | `"1 star".."5 stars"` | +0.11 (33/40) | +0.11 (33/40) |
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent` | +0.01 (31-32/40) | +0.01 (31/40) |
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | `"1".."10"`, rescaled | -0.79 (11/40) | -0.79 (11/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | words | -0.02 (39/40) | -0.02 (39/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | `"1".."5"` | -0.00, abs 0.17 (34/40) | -0.09, abs 0.09 (37/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | `"1 star".."5 stars"` | -0.15 (34/40) | -0.14 (34/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent` | -0.18 (33/40) | -0.18 (34/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | `"1".."10"`, rescaled | -0.25 (29/40) | -0.26 (28-31/40) |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | `"0".."4"` severity | +0.27 (7/10) | +0.22 (8/10) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | words | +0.03 (40/40) | +0.04 (40/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `"1".."5"` | -0.06 (39/40) | -0.07 (39/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `"0 stars".."4 stars"` | +0.25 (28-31/40) | +0.24 (28-31/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `"1 star".."5 stars"` | -0.07 (38/40) | -0.07 (37-38/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent` | -0.15 (35/40) | -0.14 (35/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `"1".."10"`, rescaled | -0.41 (21-23/40) | -0.42 (22-23/40) |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | `"0".."4"` severity | -0.39 (7/10) | -0.09 (9/10) |

Only the `"1".."5"` and `"0".."4"` rows change their prompt or labels. The other rows send byte-identical prompts on both builds, so their differences are run-to-run noise. The gateway already labelled `"1".."5"` as `1` to `5` on main.

On `/v1/decisions` a score keeps letter labels on both builds.

Letter keys out of order, correct of 24:

| path · model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| systemone · Qwen3-4B | 1 | 24 |
| decisions · Qwen3-4B | 1 | 24 |
| systemone · DiffusionGemma | 17-18 | 24 |
| gateway · DiffusionGemma | 15-17 | 24 |
| systemone and decisions · d1-3B | 24 | 24 |

Liquid d1-3B through `/v1/systemone` reads the same on main and this PR: words -0.02 (40/40), `"1".."5"` -0.10 (34/40), `"1 star".."5 stars"` -0.07 (37/40), `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent` -0.18 (33/40), `"1".."10"` rescaled -0.48 (23/40). The same branch with the d1 strategy reading `question.labels` instead of the checkpoint's positional digits reads `"1".."5"` at -0.40 (23/40).

With `C, A, D, B` options, main shows d1 the codes `A "C"`, `B "A"`, ...; d1 still answered 24/24, and this PR shows `C "C"`, `A "A"`, ....

Servers, one per GPU, with the PR branch and with main:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --max-model-len 4096 --enable-prefix-caching
vllm serve LiquidAI/d1-3B --max-model-len 8192 --mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA
vllm serve google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 64}' \
    --max-logprobs 32 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192
python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py \
    --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it --canvas 64
```

Each request asks one question, eight requests in flight at a time. The decision strategies turn Qwen3 thinking off.

</details>

## Details

Root cause: `build_question()` took `qtype.label_set[: len(options)]` for every question, `make_read_question()` took `LABELS[: len(options)]`, and the gateway's `parse_schema()` took `1..n` or `A..Z`. Nothing compared a label with the name next to it.

The own labels are a subset of the existing label table (digits and `A` to `Z`), so the token ids the strategies resolve at startup cover them.

`LiquidStrategy` builds the score legend and readout from `question.type.label_set`, not `question.labels`. The checkpoint's `prompt.py` writes `{i} {name}` with `i` from 0, and own-digit labels read worse on d1-3B (above).

The gateway copies the rule instead of importing it. It imports only the standard library, `pybase64` and `transformers`; importing vLLM would tie the example to a vLLM version. A shared test table pins the two copies together.

Limits:

- Own labels apply only when every name is a label. `"1 star".."5 stars"` and `poor, 2, 3, 4, excellent` keep positional labels, so a model may still answer with a level's own digit.
- The built-in endpoint still allows at most 10 score levels.
- Plus/minus grades (`A+`, `A`, `A-`) and choices that mix letters with other names (`["B", "Other"]` shows `A: B`) still clash with letter labels in the prompt.
- The built-in prompt shows an own-digit level as its digit alone (`1`); the gateway keeps `1: 1`.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

</details>
